en: The Jātaka:
Catukkanipāta, Pucimandavagga (The Chapter on the Nimba Tree)
10. The Saccakajātika Jātaka:
“Truly, he who spoke the truth danced, for by his word he gave up the mountain.”
“What benefit was there for one who gave away his own body,
that you spoke with words of giving a mountain?
“Speak only what you would do;”
One should not speak of that which one would not do;
the wise discern the one who speaks without acting.
“O Prince, let there be homage to you;
you are established in truth and righteousness,
even though calamity has befallen you.”
The mind finds delight in truth.
“That which is the fame of the poor man for his poverty,
and of the wealthy man for his wealth— ”
For she is his supreme wife,
among all women, even for one possessed of wealth.
Thus ends the *Succaja-jātaka*, the tenth.
The second chapter: The Pucimanda Chapter.
Its summary verse:
Now, the thief, Sakka, Khantivāra, ...
A harsh life is better than living poorly;
it is more pleasant to die while practicing self-restraint, generosity,
virtue, and the wearing of antelope skins— these ten qualities.
